title: Let You Sit With Me
style: Intimate bedroom singer-songwriter, close soft mezzo-soprano vocal with natural conversational phrasing, fingerpicked acoustic guitar and restrained felt piano, subtle room noise and warm tape texture. Start spare and confessional, let a gentle bass pulse and brushed percussion enter gradually, open the chorus with a little more harmony, then strip back to voice and guitar for the unresolved final lines. Human, understated mix with audible breath and no glossy polish.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I wake with yesterday still on my sleeves
The sink is full, the mail leans by the door
I know the list, I know what each thing means
I watch another little screen instead

[Pre-Chorus]
I can name the pattern after it has passed
I can trace the cost in every quiet room
But knowing isn't moving, and the hours move fast
While I make a smaller world to disappear into

[Chorus]
I didn't choose the day I learned to grow
It came like weather, and I stayed beneath it
I see the things I owe, the hurt I leave behind
I see the first step, still I can't begin it
If there's a way to carry what is mine
I haven't found it on my own

[Verse 2]
Some page explains the lock inside my head
A word that might make all this less a flaw
One part of me wants shelter in the name
One part says a name won't open any door

[Pre-Chorus]
And shame can keep me frozen just as long
As any reason I can write down clean
I know the answer when the moment's gone
But not the way to do it while I'm in it

[Chorus]
I didn't choose the day I learned to grow
It came like weather, and I stayed beneath it
I see the things I owe, the hurt I leave behind
I see the first step, still I can't begin it
If there's a way to carry what is mine
I haven't found it on my own

[Bridge]
Maybe I need a hand beside the table
Not another verdict, not a perfect plan
Stay with me while I make one small thing happen
Help me start before I understand

[Outro]
The sink is full, the mail leans by the door
I'll put one envelope where I can see
I don't know how to do this all alone
But maybe I can let you sit with me
